name: United States Postal Service

profile.address: 900, North Alameda Street, New Chinatown, Civic Center, Chinatown, Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, California, 90012
profile.reading:
The Terminal Annex is a large historic post office building at 900 North Alameda Street in downtown Los Angeles, next to Union Station and the city's Chinatown and Civic Center districts. Built between 1938 and 1940, it is recognized as a California Historical Landmark and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its architecture and its role in the city's mail handling history during the mid twentieth century, when Los Angeles grew into one of the country's major postal hubs.

The building is owned and operated by the United States Postal Service, an independent federal agency, and its primary documented function remains postal. Mail processing and related USPS operations tied to its historic role as a rail adjacent terminal facility are what the public record actually describes. Some equipment and engineering references associated with the building point to IT and network infrastructure being housed within it alongside its postal functions, which would be consistent with USPS's general practice of folding data and network equipment into its existing nationwide real estate footprint rather than building purpose made data center campuses for every regional need. That practice does not make the Terminal Annex primarily a data center, however, and no USPS publication, capacity disclosure, or independent source describes this site as a dedicated data center facility with its own power, cooling, or tenancy profile. Its public identity, landmark status, and available documentation all center on its postal and historic architectural significance rather than any computing infrastructure it may also contain.

reading:
The United States Postal Service is an independent establishment of the federal executive branch, and it does run a large internal IT estate supporting mail tracking, retail, logistics and administration. Neither of those facts is why it appears here. The single facility attached to this operator record is the Los Angeles Terminal Annex at 900 North Alameda Street, and the data centre inside that building is not operated by the Postal Service at all.

The Terminal Annex was completed in 1940 as the central mail processing facility for Los Angeles, next to Union Station on the edge of Chinatown and the Civic Center. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places under reference 85000131 and is a California Historical Landmark. The Postal Service later sold it. CoreSite states on its own site that the building was constructed in 1940 as the central mail processing facility for Los Angeles, that it purchased the former postal annex, and that it retrofitted the structure into a data centre, which it markets as LA2 with more than 432,000 square feet. PeeringDB lists facility 363 as CoreSite Los Angeles LA2 at 900 N. Alameda, Los Angeles, California 90012, carrying the CLLI code LSANCAVJ, recording CoreSite as the property owner, and giving coordinates within about ten metres of the point stored for this row. CoreSite Realty Corporation's Schedule III real estate disclosure, in its annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2020, carries LA2 at a gross book value of 294.4 million dollars, of which 18.7 million dollars is land, with a date of acquisition of 2010. A land basis of that kind is fee ownership of a building, not a tenancy inside somebody else's post office.

The attribution error is traceable, and it was not carelessness. The OpenStreetMap way for the Terminal Annex was drawn in 2009 and carried amenity=post_office with a Postal Service operator tag for well over a decade. On 26 April 2023, changeset 135363806 added telecom=data_center along with the CLLI code, with a comment noting that the Terminal Annex is also CoreSite LA2, and citing PeeringDB facility 363 as its source. The mapper recorded exactly the right thing. The operator tag, however, still named the Postal Service, because postal operations continue in part of the building, and an automated harvest that reads the telecom tag and the operator tag together manufactures a USPS data centre that does not exist.

The Postal Service does maintain genuine computing infrastructure, including engineering and information technology facilities and regional network sites, but none of that is established for this address by any Postal Service publication, and no capacity figure of any kind has been published for a USPS data centre here. What is established is a 1940 mail terminal that CoreSite bought and converted. This row should be read as a CoreSite carrier hotel and colocation building with a residual postal tenant, not as federal data centre capacity.
